content: Dill oil is an essential oil derived from the seeds or leaves and stems (commonly referred to as dill weed) of the dill plant. When combined with water, it can be used to create a preparation known as dill water. The dill plant, also called Indian dill, originates from Southwest Asia. It is an annual or biennial herb that can grow up to 1 meter (approximately 3 feet) in height. The plant is characterized by its green, feathery leaves and umbels of small yellow flowers, which eventually produce tiny, compressed seeds. Historically, dill was highly regarded by ancient civilizations such as the Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans, who referred to it as Anethon, a term that influenced its botanical name. The common name dill is derived from the Anglo-Saxon words dylle or dylla, which later evolved into dill. These terms mean to lull, reflecting the plant's soothing properties. During the Middle Ages, dill was even used as a charm to ward off witchcraft. From 812 AD onward, under the directive of Charlemagne, Emperor of France, dill was extensively cultivated and became widely used, particularly as a culinary herb. Dill oil is recognized for its distinct grass-like aroma, pale yellow color, and watery viscosity. In terms of its applications, dill oil is not used in the preparation of gripe water, which is typically made from the fresh herb and administered to infants and children for colic or other digestive issues, as the oil itself is too potent for such purposes. However, dill oil is known to provide relief for adults experiencing digestive problems, such as flatulence, constipation, and hiccups. It is also believed to alleviate feelings of being overwhelmed, calm headaches, and reduce excessive sweating caused by nervous tension. Additionally, dill oil may stimulate milk production in breastfeeding mothers and support the healing of wounds. The extraction of dill oil is achieved through steam distillation, primarily from the seeds of the plant, although the entire herb—whether fresh or partially dried—can also be used in the process.
